findings_to_judge.finding: Sell-side consensus for Q2 2026 is still $5.49m revenue (5 analysts, expecting +27.4% sequential growth) and -$0.16 EPS, six weeks after Nanox itself pre-announced Q2 revenue of 'approximately $4.0 to $4.1 million' -- a sequential decline; the headline on 2026-09-09 is therefore a mechanically guaranteed ~26% revenue miss.

Nanox has an unquantified 'comprehensive impairment assessment across all of its assets, including but not limited to long-lived assets and goodwill' still incomplete as of 2026-08-06, sitting against $57.364m of net intangibles and $30.551m of net PP&E at 2026-03-31 -- $88.0m of impairable carrying value versus a ~$68m market cap -- and it lands in the first quarter reported by a CFO who started 2026-08-01.

The baseline's reaction history is wrong in a way that matters: the -44.01% on 2026-06-25 and -24.39% on 2026-04-20 were real earnings prints (Q1 2026 and FY2025), independently confirmed as a -43.99% post-release move, so this name's actual earnings base rate is 2-for-2 double-digit declines, not a 6.52% median.

Offsetting and pointing the other way: the four things that caused the last two collapses are all already disclosed -- 2026 guidance withdrawn, going-concern doubt introduced, Korea restructuring announced with a $17.5m charge taken, and Q2 revenue and the $31.4m 6/30 cash balance pre-announced -- while management has run a positive-news cadence into the print (Intel/OpenVINO 8/10, UK reseller 8/18, New England distributor 9/4) and needs a shareholder majority on 2026-09-17 to lift authorized capital by 50m shares.
